thesis: IOI Properties has improving operating cash, but the bear outweighs it with distorted headline valuation and financed expansion. Fair-value/remeasurement gains account for 51.31% of PBT, while borrowings rose approximately 29.4% and net debt reached RM21.818bn before leases. The 8.54x trailing multiple therefore supplies weak downside protection; speculative future asset conversion does not yet outweigh current financing exposure.
strongest_counterexample: CFO rose to RM2.391bn from RM1.060bn and left RM1.780bn after the specified property/land/equipment spend before acquisitions and interest, so the asset base has a real cash-producing engine.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable annual operating cash after specified asset spend, acquisition/deposit outlays and interest positive without net borrowing drawdowns would weaken the financing-dependence ruling.
Net debt below RM21.818bn alongside year-on-year profit growth excluding fair-value/JV remeasurement gains would undermine the leveraged-headline-value objection.
decisive_factors: Improved CFO is accepted but expansion required RM3.258bn net borrowing drawdowns.
Estimated 17.71x forward earnings is materially less forgiving than gain-supported trailing cheapness.
